first_in_archive: The Things I Used To Do

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **New Potato Caboose** (3 reviews, 1 other source): This is the last known performance of the song; Reviewer calls this performance sublime [1][4][8][10]
- **He Was a Friend of Mine** (2 reviews): Very mellow, a sweet follow-up to the opener; Reviewer finds this the prettiest version heard, with careful dynamics, strong Jerry vocals and thoughtful lead guitar solos [8][13]
- **Dancin' In The Streets** (1 review): The jam shows the band listening to each other very closely, among the best Dead playing [9]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Runs nearly 35 minutes with Wayne Ceballos on vocals; the reviewer ranks it with the era's best versions [4]
- **The Things I Used To Do** (1 other source): The only known performances of this and Who's Lovin' You Tonight involving the Dead; Bishop plays without Garcia [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Things I Used To Do**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **Who's Lovin' You Tonight**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]

## The recordings

- **gd69-06-08.sbd.cotsman.19285.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 117 min; rated 4.37/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording quality drops slightly after Me and My Uncle; Audio is crisp and clean for a tape this old [10][11]
- **gd1969-06-08.sbd.thecore.4512.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 121 min; rated 3.29/5 by 7 [2]. Said about its sound: High-quality stereo soundboard with an excellent mix; First set sounds clearer with slighter hiss than the second set; a few faint pops in set two [2][15]
- **gd1969-06-08.123986.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 120 min; rated 3.6/5 by 10 [3]

## Around the show

- Elvin Bishop sings a couple of his own songs with the band in the second set; Joplin sat in the night before [4]
- Reviewer thinks this is the show Phil describes in his book, seeing a rainbow bridge of light and musical notes between himself and Jerry [6]
- Pigpen and Elvin trade banter throughout the guest segment, including between verses of The Things I Used To Do [11]
- Second set opens with a long Lovelight featuring Wayne Ceballos; Me and My Uncle closes the first set [12]
- Elvin Bishop sits in on The Things I Used To Do and Who's Lovin' You Tonight [12]
- Lovelight features Wayne Ceballos on vocals without Pigpen; exact second-set personnel is unclear [1]
- Bishop and Ceballos join for the first three second-set songs; Ceballos sings Lovelight, Bishop sings two and plays lead guitar [2]
- Reviewer finds it merely interesting and follows Jerry's lead, far behind the 5-6-70 version with its three big peaks [8]
- Prefers it to 5/6/70, which is slower and stretched at 17 minutes; this one is fast and focused [9]
- Reviewer considers this version one of the best ever [10]
- Not the Byrds' song of the same title; it shares the tune, but theirs was about JFK [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-06-08.sbd.cotsman.19285.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Litfin and J. Cotsman; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1969-06-08.sbd.thecore.4512.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MR>C>D>CD>SHN [2]. Also: The two sets come from different recording media, though the lineage is uncertain [2]
- **gd1969-06-08.123986.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat [3]
